chapter: Marriages, Tong Funeral and Liberation Music
title: Charlie Haden and the Liberation Music Orchestra
summary: She knew Charlie from Los Angeles, shared tastes in Shostakovich and Satie, and arranged his songs for the Liberation Music Orchestra after hearing Tong Funeral.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Talk a little bit more about Charlie Haden of course, the Liberation Orchestra, Music Orchestra. What, you know... of course you knew Charlie from the Ornette days, right?
Yeah. I knew Charlie when he was only eighteen.
He just came to Los Angeles. And we became good friends because we had the same taste in music. And he had that theatrical thing going too.
If you’ll notice the movies, records he made - the movies... [laughs], the records he made recently were about movie music.
And maybe that’s why we both went to Los Angeles or something. We shared the same taste in music, we liked the same composers. We liked Shostakovich, we loved
Shostakovich. And... who else did we like... Ah! Erik Satie.

Again, a bunch of very theatrical people. But we liked the same music, we liked the same notes. It came down to I liked E-flat, well I prefer D. No, D-flat is better. You know, we just... everything was just... everything we shared, or argued in the tiniest increment so that it was a sharing, to even the argument. So when he went with Ornette east, I came later with Paul Bley. And Charlie heard A Genuine Tong Funeral and called me, saying “I need you to do an album for me.” And I said, “Ok, great.” And he gave me the songs that he wanted to do. A lot of it in the “Spanish Civil War” and all that, and I made arrangements of them.
And that first album was... 1969? Liberation Music Orchestra Impulse.
I don’t have the titles in front of me, do you recall some of the titles on them? It may be an unfair question to ask.

Well I... I think I wrote something called... no I don’t remember. I don’t know. I wrote a tune, and Charlie had a tune, and the rest was... just music that we did arrangements of, I think. I haven’t listened to it in forever. I forget.
